clue.text: Exact money

definitions.meaning: to exact is to demand or extort, as an extortioner does with threats
the payment handed over to an extortioner is itself called by this name

explanation.surface: A request for the precise sum, to the penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' looks like an adjective (precise), but it is the verb 'to extort'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion by threat is the verb sense; the hush money paid over is the noun sense.

clue.text: Bottle opener and drinks in packs

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word bottle is taken, as an opener comes first

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer

explanation.surface: Someone opens a bottle and the drinks arrive in multipacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bales are large tied bundles, so packs of hay or cotton.

clue.text: Amenity switched to an unspecified date

indicators.note: switched means the letters of amenity are changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: A facility's booking moved to a date not yet fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at whatever moment, so at a date not fixed in advance.

clue.text: A card cheat may be so described

definitions.text: A card cheat may be so described

parts.words: A card cheat may be so described
parts.note: the word is both the jack in a pack of cards and a dishonest rogue

explanation.definitionFit: The playing card also called the jack bears this name, and it also means a rascal.

clue.text: It goes up with inflation

parts.note: inflation here is filling with gas, not rising prices; a gas-filled craft rises

explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible balloon flies once its envelope is filled with lighter-than-air gas.

clue.text: Soldier's an expert swimmer

definitions.meaning: a soldier of the ..., a cavalry regiment of the British Household Cavalry; the 's stands for is
a strong swimmer employed to rescue bathers at a beach or pool

explanation.surface: A soldier who is also a capable swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Life Guards are a British cavalry regiment guarding the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Life Guards regiment, and also a rescuer patrolling beaches.

clue.text: Unfinished aircraft design

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: A half-built aeroplane on the drawing board.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or drawing for something to be made.

clue.text: Saucepan's ready for cooking what this has killed

definitions.text: Saucepan's ready for cooking what this has killed

parts.note: a pot is a saucepan, with the possessive s kept
a pan that is hot is ready to cook in

explanation.surface: The saucepan is heated, waiting for whatever the hunter has bagged.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a shot taken just to get something for the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a shot fired simply to bag game for the cooking pot, rather than for sport.

clue.text: Commercial address brings high esteem

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, shortened to ad
an oration is a formal speech or address

explanation.surface: A speech promoting a product earns great respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep admiration or worship, so very high regard.

clue.text: Don't cheat in two forms of leisure activity

parts.note: play is recreation, and a fair (funfair) is an outing for amusement
play is recreation, and a fair (funfair) is an outing for amusement

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay honest in a couple of pastimes.
explanation.definitionFit: To act honestly and by the rules is the idiom here, the opposite of cheating.

clue.text: Think in depth

definitions.meaning: to work out or understand something by thought
a unit of measure for water depth, six feet

explanation.surface: Ponder something deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to grasp by thinking; the noun is a nautical unit of six feet of depth.

clue.text: Aim ambitiously for praise, being wretched

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters of praise are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone craving applause while feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's hopes on a lofty goal.

clue.text: Gets more than one's share of froth with this measure of alcohol

parts.note: to hog is to take more than one's fair portion
the head on a beer is its froth

explanation.surface: A greedy drinker grabbing the foam off a large serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask, and a liquid measure for beer or wine of around 54 gallons.

clue.text: Saucy antics?

parts.note: playful leaps are antics, and the pickled flower buds of the same name go into sauces

explanation.definitionFit: Capers are frolics, and also the pickled buds used in tartare sauce.

clue.text: Enter game play, making contract

indicators.note: play suggests the letters of enter game are moved about freely

explanation.surface: Joining a sporting fixture by signing on the dotted line.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding pact between parties.

clue.text: Dismiss ministers, a sign of contrition

parts.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: A prime minister fires the cabinet, as a show of penitence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' suggests government, but it means clergymen, known collectively as the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric worn, with ashes, as a traditional show of penitence.

clue.text: Worker in the prairie producing fruit

indicators.note: in means one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a prairie is a great grassy plain
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A farmhand out on the prairie grows a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy banana-like fruit cooked as a vegetable in the tropics.

clue.text: Censorious to a dangerous degree?

definitions.meaning: at a point of crisis, as with a patient whose condition is grave

explanation.surface: Faultfinding taken too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Faultfinding is one sense; being in a grave, crisis state is the other.

clue.text: Enormous disaster struck it

definitions.meaning: the famous liner that hit an iceberg and sank in 1912

explanation.surface: A huge catastrophe hit something.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic is the adjective sense; the ill-fated liner of 1912 is the other.

clue.text: It makes one wild what people do when they retire

definitions.text: what people do when they retire

indicators.note: makes is read as forming something new out of the letters of one wild

explanation.surface: Something drives a person mad, and that is just how people behave on retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' here is going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going to bed and reclining there.

clue.text: Runaway affairs?

parts.note: not elopements but channels that let water run away

explanation.definitionFit: Sewers and gutters carry waste water off.

clue.text: American detained by courts in European country

indicators.note: detained by means held inside the other word

parts.note: atria are courtyards, the plural of atrium

explanation.surface: A US citizen held by the judiciary somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law; it means courtyards, ATRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked state of central Europe with Vienna as its capital.

clue.text: Star of the Magic Circle?

parts.note: not a famous conjuror but the five-pointed star drawn in a circle as a magical symbol

explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is the London society of stage magicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram, a five-pointed star used in magic, often inside a circle.

clue.text: One takes no end of cash in, finishing with nothing

definitions.text: One takes no end of cash in, finishing with nothing

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gambling house rakes in money until the punter is left penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes a gambling house that takes in money until you have none.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling establishment that takes in stakes, leaving many players broke.

clue.text: Expenses legally incurred

parts.note: the sums a court may order a losing party to pay towards a lawsuit

explanation.definitionFit: Legal expenses awarded against a losing party in court are known by this term.

clue.text: Relative found somewhere in the south of France, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means a word said out loud is matched by its sound

parts.words: somewhere in the south of France
parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A family member turns up on the Riviera, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Show preference for old penthouse

definitions.meaning: penthouse originally meant a shed sloping against a wall

explanation.surface: Favouring an antique rooftop flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A penthouse once meant a sloping-roofed shed against a wall, not a luxury flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed whose roof slopes against a wall is the older meaning of penthouse.

clue.text: Said to be celebrated

definitions.meaning: kept or marked, as a festival is kept

explanation.surface: Reported to be famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is one sense; to keep a holiday or ritual is the other.

clue.text: Ring starts nervous reaction in the ear

indicators.note: starts means the first piece comes at the front of the second

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A ringing noise sets off a twitch in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the anatomical adjective for the ear and hearing.

clue.text: Workers given fish — a gesture of goodwill

parts.note: hands are workers, as farmhands
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: The staff receive a fish as a friendly gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping palms is a common greeting or sign of agreement.
